stubBoundary.frozenSource: SemiconFab/twin.html @ d76378c; benchmark/routes.json and twin/layout-default.json are the pinned assets the frozen page fetches at runtime (see source-manifest.json).
stubBoundary.execution: Only character-for-character frozen slices are executed inside node:vm; every emitted number comes from original source code.
stubBoundary.three: THREE is a recording stub: Vector3 (set/copy/clone/lerpVectors/distanceTo), BufferAttribute, BufferGeometry, LineBasicMaterial. The FOUP group and trail line are declared recording objects shaped exactly as frozen initWaferFollowSystem builds them; no rendering happens.
stubBoundary.camera: camera.position / controls.target are plain Vector3 recording objects; camera.lookAt and controls.update are no-ops (they do not feed any recorded value).
stubBoundary.dom: document.getElementById returns recording elements (textContent / style.width / classList) so the frozen HUD, countdown and dot updates are inspectable data.
stubBoundary.clock: performance.now() is the declared deterministic clock. requestAnimationFrame fires on the declared 16 ms frame grid; setTimeout/setInterval run on a deterministic virtual event queue (ties by registration order). The frozen Tour uses performance.now + RAF + a 100 ms setInterval countdown; the frozen Wafer derives its own dt from performance.now with Math.min(dt, 0.1).
stubBoundary.randomness: No Math.random draws exist on these frozen code paths; the fixture records the declared LCG seed (42) for harness reproducibility.
stubBoundary.tourState: Tour module-level state (isCinematicTourActive, tourTimeoutId, tourCountdownInterval, currentTourWaypointIndex, activeCameraAnimId, currentFabLevel) is declared in the sandbox with the frozen initial values; CINEMATIC_WAYPOINTS is sliced from source.
stubBoundary.crossFeature: Tour/wafer mutual exclusion is stubbed: the tour sandbox declares an inactive waferFollowState (so startCinematicTour skips closeWaferFollow), and the wafer sandbox leaves stopCinematicTour undefined (typeof guards skip it). Cross-feature exclusivity is not part of these timing vectors.
stubBoundary.waferState: waferFollowState / foupGroup / waferTrailLine / waferTrailHistory / waferLastFrameTime are declared sandbox state; waferFollowState is initialised to the frozen literal values, then the declared session setup positions the FOUP on waypoint 0 and primes waferLastFrameTime exactly like toggleWaferFollowPanel does.
stubBoundary.routeData: computeWaferWaypoints is executed against the pinned benchmark/routes.json + twin/layout-default.json route/layout data that the page fetches. The trace uses a declared 5-step prefix of each product route (the full pinned routes have 120/104/92 steps) so a fixed-time trace stays bounded; waypoint x/z are still chosen by the frozen round-robin against the full layout tool list.
stubBoundary.seekAdvance: Frozen source has no seek/scrub for the wafer follow flow: the wafer UI exposes play/pause, speed 1x/4x/16x, replay, product select and camera follow only (twin.html:955-1036, 18503-18616). Fast-forward is setWaferSpeed scaling dur = 2.0 / speed (18293); replayWaferRoute resets index/stepTimer/trail. The Tour advances via timer callbacks + tweenCamera RAF frames; next/prev jump waypoints. There is no seek in either flow and none was invented.
stubBoundary.dtClamp: updateWaferFollowFrame computes dt = Math.min((performance.now() - waferLastFrameTime) / 1000, 0.1); the declared stall trace feeds one 500 ms frame gap to exercise the 0.1 s clamp.
stubBoundary.hudLanguage: HUD text is captured with currentLang = "en" (the frozen HUD renders English for any non-zh language); Tour HUD titles are captured in English for the same reason.
